entry.title: Affective Valence as the Interoceptive Rate of Change of Jacobian Scale. Affect is widely held to depend on interoception.
entry.summary:
Affect is widely held to depend on interoception. This paper proposes that valence is the rate at which interoception moves a self-sustaining system's responsiveness relative to its terminal set (roughly, death). Responsiveness is formalised as the scale of the system's Jacobian and interoception as its internal inputs: receptors, signals and forecasts of its energy reserve.

Source: arXiv Quantitative Biology & Materials (q-bio, mtrl-sci) · Tags: #bioinformatics #genomics-proteins #neuroscience #complex-systems

entry.title: GOLDEN: Gene expression and allele-informed decomposition for genetic heterogeneity in spatial transcriptomic data
entry.summary:
Motivation Spatial transcriptomics (ST) enables exploration of cellular interactions, including immune responses. However, current methods rely on pathologists, with limitations in addressing genetic heterogeneity, where niches harboring nonclonal cells, including placental or allograft tissues, are present. Deciphering these interindividual mixtures remains challenging.

Source: bioRxiv Bioinformatics Preprints · Tags: #bioinformatics #genomics-proteins

entry.title: RDEmbed: A Sentence-Embedding Framework for Rare Disease Phenotype Representation and Phenotypic Similarity Analysis
entry.summary:
Accurate phenotypic characterization of patients with rare diseases is essential for improving diagnosis, patient matchmaking, and gene discovery. Conventional ontology driven approaches based on the Human Phenotype Ontology (HPO) enable structured phenotype comparison but often limited by the incomplete annotations and reduced ability to capture the contextual information contained in free-text clinical narratives. We present RDEmbed, a sentence embedding framework that learns patient phenotype representations directly from rare disease case reports for similarity analysis.

Source: bioRxiv Bioinformatics Preprints · Tags: #bioinformatics #genomics-proteins #rag

entry.title: Fibres and glasses are competing material states in protein condensation
entry.summary:
Nature Physics, Published online: 20 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41567-026-03415-z Fibres are thought to emerge from a dense protein condensate ageing into a glassy state. It is now shown that protein fibres and glassy condensates may result from two competing ageing pathways.

Source: Nature Physics · Tags: #quantum-physics #optics-photonics #genomics-proteins

entry.title: Hybrid modeling for improved structure prediction of large protein complexes

entry.title: HDOCK-Multimer: improved structure prediction of large protein complexes by integrating docking and combinatorial assembly
entry.summary:
Nature Computational Science, Published online: 14 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43588-026-01062-1 This study presents HDOCK-Multimer, a general framework for structure prediction of large protein complexes by integrating ab initio docking and combinatorial assembly, substantially outperforming state-of-the-art methods.
